name: Petting cats and dogs
summary: Friendly cats and dogs can be praised, petted and fed treats, which IGN says boosts Focus and the Criminal Profile.
body: IGN says a friendly animal is first focused on with L2/LT and then praised; an animal that does not want to be petted will often come closer if the praise is repeated.
IGN says the character crouches once the animal sits, and the pet is then given with Triangle (X on Xbox).
According to IGN, up to two pet treats can be fed to an animal on top of petting, and treats are sold at the till of grocery and convenience stores.
IGN says petting and feeding cats and dogs gives a Focus boost, a small amount of progress toward the next Focus level and points toward a professional Criminal Profile.
GamesRadar+ says the same L2/LT focus on an unidentified animal also offers Study, which adds it to the animal collection, and Scold.
GamesRadar+ points to a cat that works in the Key Lento Mini Mart as one to meet early in Chapter 1, and says only domestic animals can be petted.

name: Relationship levels
summary: IGN names the four relationship levels, from Running On Empty to Hot Together, and the gameplay that raises or lowers them.
body: IGN gives the four levels, lowest first, as Running On Empty (a broken purple heart), Not So Hot (a half-broken gradient heart), Crazy In Love (a pink heart) and Hot Together (a flaming heart).
IGN says the level shows at the bottom of the Jason & Lucia tab of the map screen and on the heart between the two portraits in the relationship quick-menu, opened by holding Right on the D-pad.
IGN says changes show as a purple broken heart with a minus, a pink heart with a plus, or a flaming heart for a big gain, mostly tied to story moments.

IGN lists invitations to hang out, hugs and kisses (L2/LT then Square/X on the heart prompt), talking while driving (hold Up), dancing together at clubs, holding hands (hold R2/RT), handing over food or drinks, exercising and committing crimes together as raising it.
IGN says ignoring calls, texts or greetings, long spells apart and driving off without the partner lower it, and that Hot Together needs both characters to contribute.

IGN says the two can be intimate at Crazy In Love or Hot Together, with a cooldown of at least a couple of real-world hours, and that no other character can be romanced and no sex workers can be solicited.

name: Wanted star colours
summary: IGN explains five looks for the wanted stars, from grey (reported, unseen) to red outlines (police on alert but no longer matching you).
body: IGN says the wanted level follows what is reported, not what is done: a crime seen by police, a witness's call, a mistaken report, or a crime big enough for dispatch to respond at once, such as explosions, trespassing in high-security areas or stealing a plane.

IGN says grey stars mean a crime has been reported and police are coming with a description but have not seen the player; more grey stars need more reports, and stars also turn grey when police lose sight.
IGN says unfilled stars with a white outline mean an incident is known but not who did it, for example when heat icons were cleared before being seen or gunfire was heard but not seen.

IGN says solid white stars mean police have eyes on the player and are in full pursuit; they often use Tasers on an unarmed suspect, and shooting tyres or yellow non-lethal spots raises the level more slowly than shots to the body or head.

IGN says solid red stars mean police have lost the player but are hunting someone matching the heat icons shown, while red-outlined stars mean they know a crime happened in the area but the player no longer matches; the area is outlined and shaded red on the map.
IGN says a police scanner, unlocked in an early Chapter 1 story mission, relays what dispatch knows, including when a helicopter leaves to refuel.

name: Tolls, turn signals and the horn
summary: IGN's beginner tips on driving: $5 tolls, turn signals on the D-pad, a horn that can move traffic, and a first-person phone view.
body: IGN says passing through a toll costs 5 dollars, but nothing is charged in a stolen car or a friend's vehicle.
IGN says Left and Right on the D-pad work the turn signals while driving, switching off once the turn is done.
IGN says honking with a click of the left stick can make a stalled car ahead pull out into traffic, or anger its driver.
IGN says taking out the phone while driving switches to a first-person view with the road out of focus, though full control remains.
IGN says audible GPS directions are set under Settings, Audio, GPS Voice, and that buildings with explorable interiors are outlined on the minimap and map.

name: Flipping an overturned vehicle
summary: IGN says a car on its side or roof is righted by pushing it, with a charged shove for heavier ones; small boats can be pushed back too.
body: IGN says a vehicle on its side or roof is righted on foot by walking into it to push, which can roll a light car over.
IGN says holding Square (X on Xbox) while pushing charges a hard shove that rights most cars; some need pushing from the other side or a bump from another vehicle.
IGN says the same pushing works on small boats stranded on land, nudging them back to the water.

name: Street interactions
summary: IGN's beginner tips on dealing with people in the street: shoves and slaps, knocking away a phone, rude gestures and trespassing.
body: IGN says Square (X on Xbox) out of combat gives a slap or shove that is aggressive but not lethal, turning into punches and kicks if repeated or if the other person escalates.
IGN says someone reaching for their phone to call the police can have it slapped out of their hand with Square/X, though many witnesses can still get the call through.
IGN says the interaction system (L2/LT) handles strangers who approach or odd events, and that holding R1/RB while focused on someone gives a rude gesture, with reactions varying by person.
IGN says people may shout, call the police or physically remove a character standing on their property.

IGN says lifeguard huts on Vice Beach can hold a volleyball that can be thrown at people, mostly to outrage, and that knocked-off hats and glasses that are not owned must be picked up or they are lost.
